title: Phytochemical Profiling of Non-Marketable Organs of White Onion (Allium cepa L.): A Comparative Study of Two Extraction Methods Using HPLC-DAD
content: In this research, white onion (Allium cepa L.) residual organs and extraction methods were evaluated to determine optimal recovery conditions for flavanones (naringenin, apigenin) and flavonols (quercetin, kaempferol, and galangin). Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) and decoction were compared using flower and leaf residues. Leaf decoction yielded higher concentrations of quercetin (0.33 mg g⁻¹), naringenin (0.24 mg g⁻¹), galangin (0.23 mg g⁻¹), and kaempferol (0.07 mg g⁻¹) compared to flower residues. Conversely, apigenin was highest in flower decoction (0.15 mg g⁻¹) and undetected via UAE. Phytochemical profiles were significantly influenced by both plant organ and extraction method. Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS) revealed that quercetin, galangin, and naringenin predominated in leaf residues, showing strong positive vector correlations along NMDS1 (0.508, 0.507, and 0.509, respectively), whereas apigenin exhibited a negative correlation (-0.470). NMDS2 was primarily driven by kaempferol concentration (vector score of 0.793).
